title: Making plans
goal: Talk about dates and days, say what you can and have to do, and make, accept or politely decline plans by phone or message.

notes.p: Months are a counting number + {{月|jyut6}}: {{一月|jat1 jyut6}} January, {{二月|ji6 jyut6}} February … {{十二月|sap6 ji6 jyut6}} December. The day of the month is a number + {{號|hou6}}. Say the bigger unit first: {{三月十號|saam1 jyut6 sap6 hou6}} = March 10th. Careful: February is {{二月|ji6 jyut6}}, but 'two months' is {{兩個月|loeng5 go3 jyut6}}, with {{兩|loeng5}} and a measure word. {{號|hou6}} is low and flat; don't let it rise into {{好|hou2}}.

notes.h: Weeks and days of the week
notes.p: {{星期|sing1 kei4}} and {{禮拜|lai5 baai3}} both mean 'week', and in everyday speech {{禮拜|lai5 baai3}} is very common. Days are 'week' + a number: {{禮拜一|lai5 baai3 jat1}} Monday … {{禮拜六|lai5 baai3 luk6}} Saturday; Sunday is {{禮拜日|lai5 baai3 jat6}}. 'Which day?' is {{星期幾|sing1 kei4 gei2}}. 'Next' is {{下|haa6}} and 'last' is {{上|soeng6}}: {{下個禮拜|haa6 go3 lai5 baai3}} next week, {{上個禮拜|soeng6 go3 lai5 baai3}} last week, {{下個月|haa6 go3 jyut6}} next month. You can also drop {{個|go3}}: {{下星期|haa6 sing1 kei4}}.
ex: gam1 jat6 sing1 kei4 gei2 aa3

notes.p: {{識|sik1}} = know how to, for a learned skill: {{我唔識游水|ngo5 m4 sik1 jau4 seoi2}}. Keep it high: {{食|sik6}} with a low tone means 'eat'. {{可以|ho2 ji5}} = can or may, when something is possible or allowed. {{得|dak1}} = it works, I can make it: {{我聽日唔得|ngo5 ting1 jat6 m4 dak1}}. {{會|wui5}} still means 'will'. {{要|jiu3}} before a verb = need to, have to.
ex: nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 jing1 man2 aa3
ni1 dou6 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 jing2 soeng2 aa3
lai5 baai3 luk6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3

notes.p: {{約|joek3}} = to arrange to meet someone. Invite with {{你想唔想一齊去呀？|nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 jat1 cai4 heoi3 aa3}} or with {{不如…啦|bat1 jyu4 … laa1}} from Level 6. Say yes with {{好呀！|hou2 aa3}}, and lock the plan in with {{就咁話啦|zau6 gam2 waa6 laa1}} 'it's settled'. To say no politely: apologise, give a short reason, and leave the door open with {{下次先啦|haa6 ci3 sin1 laa1}} or {{遲啲再約啦|ci4 di1 zoi3 joek3 laa1}}.
ex: 唔好意思，我嗰日唔得閒
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 go2 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4
Sorry, I'm not free that day.

notes.p: Call someone: {{打電話俾|daa2 din6 waa2 bei2}} + the person. In {{電話|din6 waa2}} the second syllable rises. Pick up the phone with {{喂？|wai2}}. Hong Kongers mix in English: {{我send WhatsApp俾你|ngo5 send WhatsApp bei2 nei5}}. {{覆|fuk1}} = reply. {{遲啲|ci4 di1}} = later on, some time soon; {{晏啲|aan3 di1}} = a bit later today. {{之前|zi1 cin4}} before and {{之後|zi1 hau6}} after go AFTER the event: {{食飯之前|sik6 faan6 zi1 cin4}}. {{先|sin1}} 'first' often goes at the very end: {{等我問吓佢先|dang2 ngo5 man6 haa5 keoi5 sin1}}.
ex: ngo5 ting1 jat6 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 nei5
I'll get back to you later.

vocab.en: what date (which day of the month)
vocab.note: {{號|hou6}} = day of the month. Don't confuse with {{幾點|gei2 dim2}} what time.

t: gam1 jat6 sing1 kei4 gei2 aa3
vocab.en: What day of the week is it today?

vocab.note: Months are just numbers: {{三月|saam1 jyut6}} March, {{十二月|sap6 ji6 jyut6}} December.
Use {{二|ji6}} here, never {{兩|loeng5}}.
Month first, then day.
A length of time takes {{兩|loeng5}} and the measure word {{個|go3}}.
Same as {{星期六|sing1 kei4 luk6}}.
{{上|soeng6}} = last, {{下|haa6}} = next.

t: nei5 gei2 si4 saang1 jat6 aa3

vocab.en: to arrange to meet / make plans with
I've made plans with a friend
vocab.note: A handy reason for saying no.

t: nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 jat1 cai4 heoi3 aa3
vocab.en: Do you want to come along?
vocab.note: Word for word: 'do you want to go together?'
Said to close a plan. {{話|waa6}} keeps its low tone here.

t: 唔好意思，我嗰日唔得閒
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 go2 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4
vocab.en: Sorry, I'm not free that day

vocab.note: A soft no that leaves the door open.
Word for word: 'wait where?'
{{晏啲|aan3 di1}} is 'a bit later today'.
Goes after the event: {{食飯之前|sik6 faan6 zi1 cin4}} before eating.
Often at the very end of the sentence.

t: dang2 ngo5 man6 haa5 keoi5 sin1
vocab.note: {{等我|dang2 ngo5}} = let me. {{佢|keoi5}} can be him or her.

vocab.en: to know how to (a learned skill)
vocab.note: High tone. {{食|sik6}} (eat) is low.

t: nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 jing1 man2 aa3
vocab.note: {{英文|jing1 man2}}: the second syllable rises in speech.

t: ni1 dou6 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 jing2 soeng2 aa3

vocab.en: Does that work? / Is that OK?

vocab.note: Before a verb: {{我要返工|ngo5 jiu3 faan1 gung1}} I have to work.
{{走|zau2}} = leave.
{{電話|din6 waa2}}: the second syllable rises. Call someone = {{打電話俾|daa2 din6 waa2 bei2}} + person.
Rising tone, for picking up the phone. Called out to get someone's attention it is {{喂|wai3}}, mid level, and can sound rude. Not a greeting in person.

t: m4 goi1, ngo5 wan2 can4 saang1
vocab.en: Hi, I'd like to speak to Mr Chan
vocab.note: {{搵|wan2}} = look for. {{陳生|can4 saang1}} = Mr Chan.

t: nei5 din6 waa2 gei2 do1 hou6 aa3

vocab.note: WhatsApp is how most of Hong Kong messages.

vocab.en: He hasn't replied to me yet
I'll get back to you later

items.en: What's the date today?
items.why: {{號|hou6}} is the day of the month. {{幾點|gei2 dim2}} asks the time.

items.en: Her birthday is in February.
items.why: Month names use the counting number: {{二月|ji6 jyut6}}. {{兩個月|loeng5 go3 jyut6}} means 'two months'.

q: nei5 ___ m4 sik1 gong2 jing1 man2 aa3
items.en: Do you speak English?
items.why: A-not-A with {{識|sik1}} (know how to): {{識唔識|sik1 m4 sik1}}. {{食|sik6}} 'eat' is the low-tone look-alike.

q: ting1 jat6 ngo5 m4 ___, ngo5 jiu3 faan1 gung1
items.en: I can't make it tomorrow; I have to work.
items.why: {{唔得|m4 dak1}} = that doesn't work for me. {{唔識|m4 sik1}} would mean you don't know how.

q: m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ting1 jat6 ___ faan1 gung1
items.en: Sorry, I have to work tomorrow.
items.why: {{要|jiu3}} before a verb = have to. {{想|soeng2}} is 'want to'.

q: ngo5 dei6 jat1 ___ heoi3 jam2 caa4 laa1
items.en: Let's go for dim sum together.
items.why: Spoken Cantonese says {{一齊|jat1 cai4}} for 'together', right before the verb. {{一共|jat1 gung6}} means 'in total'.

q: ngo5 ___ zo2 pang4 jau5 ting1 maan5 sik6 faan6
items.en: I've arranged to have dinner with a friend tomorrow night.
items.why: {{約|joek3}} = arrange to meet. {{約咗|joek3 zo2}}: the arranging is done, the dinner is tomorrow.

items.en: I'll get back to you later.
items.why: {{覆|fuk1}} = reply to someone.

q: ngo5 ting1 jat6 daa2 din6 waa2 ___ nei5
items.en: I'll call you tomorrow.
items.why: Call someone = {{打電話俾|daa2 din6 waa2 bei2}} + person: the call goes 'to' them.

q: sau1 gung1 ___, ngo5 dei6 heoi3 tai2 hei3 laa1
items.en: After work, let's go see a movie.
items.why: {{之後|zi1 hau6}} = after; {{之前|zi1 cin4}} = before. Both come after the event.

items.en: Let me ask her first.
items.why: {{先|sin1}} at the end of a sentence = 'first, before anything else'.

q: haa6 go3 ___ ngo5 heoi3 hoeng1 gong2
items.en: Next week I'm going to Hong Kong.
items.why: {{下個禮拜|haa6 go3 lai5 baai3}} = next week. 'Next year' is {{下年|haa6 nin2}}, without {{個|go3}}.

q: 唔好意思，我嗰日唔得閒，下次___啦
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 go2 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4, haa6 ci3 ___ laa1
items.en: Sorry, I'm not free that day. Maybe next time.
items.why: {{下次先啦|haa6 ci3 sin1 laa1}} is the fixed polite 'maybe next time'.

items.en: What day of the week is it today?
items.why: {{星期幾|sing1 kei4 gei2}} = which day of the week.

items.en: Sure, it's settled then.
items.why: {{啦|laa1}} closes an agreement or suggestion. {{咩|me1}} would turn it into a surprised question.

q: nei5 ho2 m4 ___ bong1 ngo5 jing2 soeng2 aa3
items.en: Could you take a photo for me?
items.why: {{可唔可以|ho2 m4 ho2 ji5}}: with a two-syllable word, only the first syllable goes before {{唔|m4}}.

items.q: Ka-yan invites you to dim sum this Saturday, and you'd love to go. You say:
opts: 唔好意思，我嗰日唔得閒
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 go2 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4
items.why: {{好呀|hou2 aa3}} accepts; asking {{幾點呀？|gei2 dim2 aa3}} moves the plan along.

items.q: A friend invites you out tomorrow, but you have to work. You politely say no:
opts: 唔好意思，我聽日要返工
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 faan1 gung1
ngo5 ting1 jat6 faan1 zo2 gung1
items.why: Apologise, then give the reason with {{要|jiu3}} 'have to'. {{咗|zo2}} can't describe tomorrow.

items.q: Your phone rings and you pick up. You say:
items.why: {{喂？|wai2}} is how everyone answers the phone.

items.q: You phone an office and want to speak to Mr Chan. You say:
opts: m4 goi1, ngo5 wan2 can4 saang1
m4 goi1, ngo5 hai6 can4 saang1
m4 goi1, ngo5 giu3 can4 saang1
items.why: {{搵|wan2}} = look for, the normal way to ask for someone on the phone. The others say you are Mr Chan, or say goodbye.

items.q: You want a new friend's phone number. You ask:
opts: nei5 din6 waa2 gei2 do1 hou6 aa3
nei5 zyu6 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3
items.why: {{電話幾多號|din6 waa2 gei2 do1 hou6}} = what's the phone number. {{今日幾號|gam1 jat6 gei2 hou6}} asks the date.

items.q: You messaged Wing yesterday, and he hasn't answered. You tell a friend:
items.why: {{佢未覆我|keoi5 mei6 fuk1 ngo5}}: he (subject) hasn't yet ({{未|mei6}}) replied to me.

items.q: Your friend suggests 7 p.m. at the MTR station, and that suits you. To confirm the plan, you say:
items.why: {{就咁話啦|zau6 gam2 waa6 laa1}} = it's settled. The others put the plan off or turn it down.

items.q: Someone asks if next Friday works. It doesn't, but you'd like to meet another time. You say:
opts: 唔好意思，我唔得。遲啲再約啦
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 m4 dak1. ci4 di1 zoi3 joek3 laa1
hou2 aa3, jat1 jin4 wai4 ding6
唔好意思，我唔識。下次見
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 m4 sik1. haa6 ci3 gin3
dak1, haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 ng5 mou5 man6 tai4
items.why: {{唔得|m4 dak1}} = doesn't work; {{遲啲再約啦|ci4 di1 zoi3 joek3 laa1}} leaves the door open. {{唔識|m4 sik1}} means 'don't know how'.

items.en: What's the date today?
full: 今日幾號呀？
gam1 jat6 gei2 hou6 aa3

items.en: See you on March 10th.
full: 我哋三月十號見
ngo5 dei6 saam1 jyut6 sap6 hou6 gin3

items.en: Do you speak English?
full: 你識唔識講英文呀？
nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 jing1 man2 aa3

items.en: I have to work tomorrow.
full: 我聽日要返工
ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 faan1 gung1

items.en: Do you want to come along?
full: 你想唔想一齊去呀？
nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 jat1 cai4 heoi3 aa3

items.en: I've arranged to have dinner with a friend tomorrow night.
full: 我約咗朋友聽晚食飯
ngo5 joek3 zo2 pang4 jau5 ting1 maan5 sik6 faan6

items.en: I'll call you tomorrow.
full: 我聽日打電話俾你
ngo5 ting1 jat6 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 nei5

items.en: He hasn't replied to me yet.
full: 佢未覆我
keoi5 mei6 fuk1 ngo5

items.en: After work, let's go see a movie.
full: 收工之後，我哋去睇戲啦
sau1 gung1 zi1 hau6, ngo5 dei6 heoi3 tai2 hei3 laa1

items.en: Let me ask her first.
full: 等我問吓佢先
dang2 ngo5 man6 haa5 keoi5 sin1

items.en: Does next Saturday work?
full: 下個禮拜六得唔得呀？
haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3

items.en: I'm not free that day. Maybe next time.
full: 我嗰日唔得閒，下次先啦
ngo5 go2 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4, haa6 ci3 sin1 laa1

items.why: {{號|hou6}} = the date. Wednesday is {{星期三|sing1 kei4 saam1}}; three o'clock is {{三點|saam1 dim2}}; the 13th would be {{十三號|sap6 saam1 hou6}}.

say: ngo5 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 heoi3 hoeng1 gong2
opts: I'm going to Hong Kong next week.
I went to Hong Kong last week.
I'm going to Hong Kong next month.
I'm going to Hong Kong this week.
I want to go to Hong Kong next week.
items.why: {{下個禮拜|haa6 go3 lai5 baai3}} = next week. Last week is {{上個禮拜|soeng6 go3 lai5 baai3}}; next month {{下個月|haa6 go3 jyut6}}.

say: nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 jau4 seoi2 aa3
opts: Do you want to go swimming?
items.why: {{識唔識|sik1 m4 sik1}} asks about a skill: do you know how to?

opts: He hasn't replied to me yet.
I haven't replied to him yet.
items.why: {{佢|keoi5}} first, so he is the one not replying; {{未|mei6}} = not yet; {{覆|fuk1}} = reply.

say: ngo5 dei6 baat3 jyut6 gau2 hou6 gin3
items.why: Month first: {{八月|baat3 jyut6}} August, then {{九號|gau2 hou6}} the 9th.

say: ting1 maan5 ngo5 m4 dak1 haan4
items.why: {{聽晚|ting1 maan5}} = tomorrow night; tonight is {{今晚|gam1 maan5}}. {{唔得閒|m4 dak1 haan4}} = not free.

say: sik6 faan6 zi1 cin4 daa2 bei2 ngo5
opts: I'll call you before we eat.
Don't call me before you eat.
items.why: {{之前|zi1 cin4}} = before; {{打俾我|daa2 bei2 ngo5}} = call me.

say: nei5 gei2 si4 dak1 haan4 aa3
items.why: {{幾時|gei2 si4}} = when; {{得閒|dak1 haan4}} = free.
{{下次先啦|haa6 ci3 sin1 laa1}} is a soft no. 'See you next time' is {{下次見|haa6 ci3 gin3}}.

say: keoi5 m4 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2
opts: She doesn't want to speak Cantonese.
items.why: {{唔識|m4 sik1}} = doesn't know how to.

s: 你禮拜六得唔得閒呀？
nei5 lai5 baai3 luk6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3

opts: dak1 haan4 aa3, zou6 me1 aa3
turns.why: Answer by repeating the key words: {{得閒|dak1 haan4}}. Then ask what's up.

s: 不如我哋一齊去飲茶啦
bat1 jyu4 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 jam2 caa4 laa1
turns.en: How about we go for dim sum together?

turns.why: Accept with {{好呀|hou2 aa3}} and ask the time. {{下次見|haa6 ci3 gin3}} is goodbye.

s: 十一點，喺地鐵站等，好唔好呀？
sap6 jat1 dim2, hai2 dei6 tit3 zaam6 dang2, hou2 m4 hou2 aa3
turns.en: Eleven o'clock, meet at the MTR station. OK?

opts: m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 m4 sik1
turns.why: {{就咁話啦|zau6 gam2 waa6 laa1}} confirms the plan. {{下次先啦|haa6 ci3 sin1 laa1}} would cancel it.

s: 喂？
wai2

opts: wai2, m4 goi1, ngo5 wan2 can4 saang1
wai2, m4 goi1, ngo5 hai6 can4 saang1
turns.why: {{我搵…|ngo5 wan2 …}} 'I'm looking for…' is how you ask for someone on the phone.

s: 佢而家唔喺度。佢遲啲打俾你，好唔好呀？
keoi5 ji4 gaa1 m4 hai2 dou6. keoi5 ci4 di1 daa2 bei2 nei5, hou2 m4 hou2 aa3
turns.en: He's not in right now. He'll call you back later, OK?

opts: m4 gan2 jiu3, ngo5 fuk1 zo2 nei5
turns.why: Someone is doing you a favour: {{唔該晒|m4 goi1 saai3}}. There's nothing to apologise for.

s: 你電話幾多號呀？
nei5 din6 waa2 gei2 do1 hou6 aa3

opts: gau2 ji6 saam1 sei3 ng5 luk6 cat1 baat3
gau2 loeng5 saam1 sei3 ng5 luk6 cat1 baat3
turns.why: Phone numbers are read digit by digit, and 2 is always {{二|ji6}} here, never {{兩|loeng5}}.

s: 我哋聽晚去睇戲，你想唔想一齊去呀？
ngo5 dei6 ting1 maan5 heoi3 tai2 hei3, nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 jat1 cai4 heoi3 aa3
turns.en: We're going to see a movie tomorrow night. Do you want to come along?

opts: 唔好意思，聽晚我要返工
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ting1 maan5 ngo5 jiu3 faan1 gung1
hou2 aa3, ngo5 tai2 zo2 laa3
唔好意思，聽晚我識返工
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ting1 maan5 ngo5 sik1 faan1 gung1
turns.why: Apologise and give the reason with {{要|jiu3}} 'have to'. {{識|sik1}} means 'know how to'.

s: 好可惜。下個禮拜六得唔得呀？
hou2 ho2 sik1. haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3
turns.en: What a pity. Does next Saturday work?

opts: dak1, haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6 mou5 man6 tai4
dak1, soeng6 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6 mou5 man6 tai4
dak1, haa6 go3 jyut6 luk6 hou6 mou5 man6 tai4
turns.why: Echo the day Wing offered: {{下個禮拜六|haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6}}. {{上個|soeng6 go3}} is 'last'; {{六號|luk6 hou6}} is the 6th of the month.

s: 好，就咁話啦！
hou2, zau6 gam2 waa6 laa1

turns.why: {{一言為定|jat1 jin4 wai4 ding6}} 'it's a deal' seals it.

s: 你幾時生日呀？
nei5 gei2 si4 saang1 jat6 aa3

opts: ngo5 sei3 jyut6 ji6 sap6 hou6 saang1 jat6
ngo5 sei3 dim2 bun3 saang1 jat6
ngo5 ji6 sap6 hou6 sei3 jyut6 saang1 jat6
turns.why: Month first, then day: {{四月二十號|sei3 jyut6 ji6 sap6 hou6}}. {{四點半|sei3 dim2 bun3}} is a clock time.

s: 我哋嗰日一齊食飯啦！
ngo5 dei6 go2 jat6 jat1 cai4 sik6 faan6 laa1
turns.en: Let's have a meal together that day!

opts: hou2 aa3! hai2 bin1 dou6 sik6 aa3
hou2 aa3! bin1 go3 saang1 jat6 aa3
turns.why: Accept and ask where. {{食咗喇|sik6 zo2 laa3}} means you've already eaten.

s: 等我問吓朋友先，遲啲覆你
dang2 ngo5 man6 haa5 pang4 jau5 sin1, ci4 di1 fuk1 nei5
turns.en: Let me ask my friends first, and I'll get back to you.

s: 你識唔識游水呀？
nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 jau4 seoi2 aa3

turns.why: Answer by repeating the verb {{識|sik1}}, high tone. {{食|sik6}} is 'eat'.

s: 禮拜日我哋一齊去游水啦！朝早九點，得唔得呀？
lai5 baai3 jat6 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 jau4 seoi2 laa1! ziu1 zou2 gau2 dim2, dak1 m4 dak1 aa3
turns.en: Let's go swimming together on Sunday! Nine in the morning — does that work?

opts: 九點唔得，十點得唔得呀？
gau2 dim2 m4 dak1, sap6 dim2 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3
九點唔識，十點識唔識呀？
gau2 dim2 m4 sik1, sap6 dim2 sik1 m4 sik1 aa3
九號唔得，十號得唔得呀？
gau2 hou6 m4 dak1, sap6 hou6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3
turns.why: Whether a time works is {{得|dak1}}, not {{識|sik1}}. Wing gave a clock time ({{點|dim2}}), not a date ({{號|hou6}}).

s: 得，冇問題。禮拜日見！
dak1, mou5 man6 tai4. lai5 baai3 jat6 gin3
turns.en: Sure, no problem. See you Sunday!

roleplay.title: Making weekend plans
roleplay.setup: Your friend Ka-yan phones you about this weekend. Agree on a day, a time and a place to meet.
roleplay.persona: You are Ka-yan, a friendly Hong Kong woman in her thirties, phoning a friend who is a beginner in Cantonese. You want to go for dim sum this weekend. You have to work on Saturday but are free on Sunday; you'd like 11 a.m. but 12 is fine too. Suggest meeting at the MTR station exit. Ask one thing at a time. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, using mostly words from levels 1-7: days of the week with lai5 baai3, dates, dak1 m4 dak1, jat1 cai4, joek3, zau6 gam2 waa6 laa1. If the learner struggles, repeat more slowly with simpler words. End by confirming the plan.

roleplay.title: Turning down an invitation
roleplay.setup: Your colleague Miss Lee invites you to her birthday dinner next Friday. You can't go that night. Decline politely and suggest another day.
roleplay.persona: You are Miss Lee, a cheerful Hong Kong office worker. Your birthday dinner is next Friday at 7 p.m. at a restaurant. You are a little disappointed if the learner can't come, but happy to meet another time: you are free next Tuesday or Wednesday evening. Ask why they can't come, then agree a new day and ask for their phone number so you can send a WhatsApp. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, mostly with words from levels 1-7. Be warm and patient; rephrase simply if the learner is stuck.
